paper_metadata.title: Investigating cognitive reserve, symptom resolution and brain connectivity in mild traumatic brain injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population and inclusion criteria. However, the sample size is very small (n=30), and there was a high refusal rate (99 individuals declined), which may introduce selection bias, particularly as the reasons for non-participation (time constraints) might correlate with symptom severity or cognitive reserve.

items.label: Source of target population

items.evidence_snippet: Patients were recruited from Danderyd University Hospital's emergency department, and all evaluations, including MRI scans, were performed on-site at the hospital.
items.reasoning: The source (Emergency Department) and the nature of the population (mTBI and orthopedic controls) are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: For the patient group, consecutive patients with mTBI significant enough to warrant a CT scan was included.
items.reasoning: While recruitment was consecutive, the high number of individuals who declined participation (99) suggests potential recruitment bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (Cognitive Reserve) was measured using two validated methods: years of education and a standardized lexical decision test for premorbid IQ.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The two measures of cognitive reserve, years of education and estimated premorbid IQ were highly correlated
items.reasoning: The study explicitly defines the PF as cognitive reserve and specifies the two metrics used.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The Swedish Lexical Decision Test was employed to evaluate the premorbid intelligence level... accounts for 48% of the variance in full-scale intelligence quote measured by the WAIS
items.reasoning: The authors use a validated neuropsychological test with known psychometric properties.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: correlation analysis with Spearman's rho was used.
items.reasoning: The PF was treated as a continuous variable in the correlation analysis, avoiding arbitrary cut-points.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using standardized, validated questionnaires (RPQ, FSS) and objective neuropsychological tests (DSST). The same methods were applied to all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study used an orthopedic control group to account for the trauma experience and measured several confounders (age, sex, psych history), the small sample size limited the ability to perform multivariable adjustment. The analysis relied on univariable correlations.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The analysis is appropriate for a pilot study (non-parametric tests, correlation), but the small sample size increases the risk of spurious findings. The authors acknowledge this as a pilot study and call for larger validation studies.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy

items.reasoning: The statistical methods are clearly laid out in the 'Analysis' section.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: To analyze the relationship between recovery over time and cognitive reserve, correlation analysis with Spearman's rho was used.
items.reasoning: The strategy is simple correlation rather than complex model building, which is appropriate for the N but limits depth.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Mann–Whitney test for nonparametric data... Wilcoxon rank sum test.
items.reasoning: Non-parametric tests are appropriate given the small sample size and likely non-normal distribution of symptom scores.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Neither improvement in RPQ-f nor DSST-f correlated with length of education... No significant correlations were found between measures of cognitive reserve... and functional connectivity
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings, reducing the risk of reporting bias.
